name: Add scripts/adr-numbers.test.ts — an invariant test pinning ADR numbers as unique
description:
**Shipped as draft PR ****[#31](https://github.com/shoptet/partner-cli/pull/31)****.**

## Why

ADRs under `doc/decisions/` are numbered `NNNN-kebab-case.md`, and that number is how prose across
`CLAUDE.md` and `doc/` refers to a decision. Two ADRs sharing a number makes every bare-number
citation ambiguous, and the repair is never local.

**This section was wrong four times before it was right**, each version well-formed and false, each
caught by a review rather than by its author. Recorded because the pattern is the lesson: "at least
four times" (a `git log --grep` skim), then "one collision plus a near-miss", then "each reaching
`develop`", then "each needed a follow-up commit". Every one was a single git command away from
being checked. The measured history:

**Two genuine in-tree collisions**, each a single tree holding two ADRs with the same number, both
caught by a human reviewer rather than by a check:

1. **0035 claimed twice.** The newer slot-layout ADR was renumbered to 0055 (`c3603f84`). Note it is
  reachable only from the local `backup/phase-2b-pre-rebase-2026-08-21` branch after the phase-1/2b
  history rewrite, so it is **not** on `origin/develop` and will not resolve on a fresh clone.
  `0035-empty-machine-config.md` is the incumbent that **kept** 0035 and is still at that path.
  Its follow-up `df9ed4e8` (which _is_ on `origin/develop`) exists purely to chase the renumber
  through three stale references — one in an ADR body and two in **code comments** under
  `packages/dev-engine/src/`, so the repair reached into source, not only into docs. That second
  commit is the cost this test prevents.
2. **0055 then claimed twice.** PR #16 renumbered it to 0062 (`26f55ab0`), landing the rename
  together with its five citing files rather than needing a follow-up. Proof it was a real in-tree
  collision and not a near-miss: `26f55ab0~1` is `eb27d5a4`, whose tree holds **both**
  `0055-id-ownership-caveat-not-a-collision-check.md` and `0055-slot-layout-lives-in-manifest.md`
  at once, and `eb27d5a4` is an ancestor of `origin/develop`.

Separately, `78d48099` is **not** a duplicate at all, and matters because it _bounds_ the guard:
0064 and 0065 were "already claimed by unmerged sibling branches", so no duplicate existed in any
single tree. A `git ls-files`-derived check on one branch structurally cannot see that case, so the
test declares it as a blind spot rather than pretending to cover it.

Nothing in this repo has reached `main` (`origin/main` is a single initial-README commit) and the
`shoptet` package has never been published — so nothing here "shipped". Nothing watched ADR
numbering either: `.claude/hooks/doc-drift.mjs` names ADR paths in its own comments but checks
nothing about numbering, and `scripts/` had no tool for it.

## What shipped

`scripts/adr-numbers.test.ts` — four assertions over one `git ls-files`-derived set (never a
maintained list, so a future ADR is covered without anyone remembering the file exists):

1. **Flatness** — `doc/decisions/` holds no nested paths, which would let two ADRs collide across
  directories while comparing clean by basename.
2. **Filename conformance** — every name matches `NNNN-kebab-case.md`. Required, not extra: without
  it a name the number regex misses drops silently out of the uniqueness set.
3. **Uniqueness** — no two ADRs share a four-digit number.
4. **Heading agreement** — each file's `# NNNN — …` H1 matches its filename.

Plus an anti-vacuity floor, so a broken enumeration fails rather than passing over an empty list.

Out of scope, deliberately: gap-freeness (a withdrawn ADR is a legitimate gap) and any crawl of
`doc/`/`CLAUDE.md` verifying that each ADR citation resolves — a larger, separate invariant.

## How it was proved

The tree was already clean (63 ADRs, `0001`–`0063`, no duplicates), so passing proved nothing. Each
assertion was reddened deliberately and reverted: a duplicate number, a malformed filename, a
mismatched heading, and — for the floor — an enumeration repointed at a path with **no tracked
files**. That last detail is load-bearing: repointing at a _populated_ directory leaves the floor
passing and reddens the conformance assertion instead, which looks like a successful perturbation
while proving nothing.

Review also found and fixed a behavioural edge: `git ls-files` prints a conflicted path once per
stage, so during an unresolved merge conflict in `doc/decisions/` the uniqueness assertion
fabricated a three-way collision against a single file and advised renumbering it. `--deduplicate`
fixes it, verified by staging three real index stages and running the suite both ways.

`pnpm verify` green (1165 package tests, 109 `scripts` tests). The changeset is intentionally empty
per `doc/versioning.md`: `packages/cli` ships `files: ["dist"]`, so `scripts/` reaches no published
artifact. Documentation landed in the same commit, in `doc/testing.md` §7 — amended from this
ticket's original `doc/development.md`, which mentions these tests only incidentally and carries no
list.
